pathways.name: Substitute teacher / paraeducator
pathways.why_it_fits: This matches your #1 priority of a flexible schedule and #2 priority of getting back to work fastest, while building directly on your Bachelor's in Elementary Education and 3 to 5 years of 2nd-grade classroom success.
pathways.what_it_needs: Light local school district onboarding and background checks; you do not need to renew your lapsed Utah teaching license first to substitute or work as a paraeducator.
pathways.how_it_fits_life: Fits school hours and 15 to 25 hours a week closely, and substitute roles let you pick which days you work. The main trade-off is that school roles are on-site rather than hybrid.
pathways.first_step: Contact your local school district HR page and book a free coaching session through Utah Dept. of Workforce Services (DWS) at jobs.utah.gov to compare district pay rates and paraeducator openings.
pathways.reality_check: Standard occupation from the pathway table, but I could not check current Utah postings or district substitute requirements without live web search. I do not have a verified Utah hourly pay figure to confirm whether local districts meet $20 to $25/hour; DWS career coaches can confirm current postings and pay.

pathways.name: Project or program coordinator
pathways.why_it_fits: Combines both of your day-to-day interests—working with people and working with information and numbers—in a varied, social role that uses your $18,000 PTA fundraiser, 140-family soccer schedule, and $95,000 budget tracking.
pathways.what_it_needs: No new degree required, though refreshing current cloud office tools and optionally exploring a beginner project certificate such as CAPM can help bridge your 12-year gap.
pathways.how_it_fits_life: Hybrid schedules are common in coordinator roles, making it the strongest match for your hybrid preference. Part-time school-hours openings (15 to 25 hours) exist in nonprofits, education organizations, and local businesses, though they take more targeted searching than full-time roles.
pathways.first_step: Visit Return Utah at returnutah.utah.gov to check upcoming cohort dates and free resume, LinkedIn, and interview workshops, and ask a DWS coach at jobs.utah.gov to help target part-time hybrid coordinator postings.
pathways.reality_check: Standard occupation from the pathway table, but I could not check current Utah postings without live web search, and part-time hybrid coordinator roles are rarer than full-time ones. I do not have a verified Utah pay figure for part-time roles; DWS career coaches can confirm current local openings and wages.

pathways.name: Event coordinator (wildcard)
pathways.why_it_fits: Directly tests your curiosity about coordinating events or community programs and running events for a company, backed by your 60-volunteer, $18,000 fall fun run and 12-team soccer league scheduling.
pathways.what_it_needs: No formal credential is usually required; a short portfolio summary of the PTA fun run and league logistics plus updated spreadsheet and scheduling software skills is enough to start.
pathways.how_it_fits_life: Fits your love of variety and busy, social environments, and some corporate or nonprofit coordinators work hybrid. However, event roles frequently require irregular, evening, or weekend hours that conflict with school-hours availability unless you focus on daytime school, nonprofit, or internal company events.
pathways.first_step: Use a DWS career coach at jobs.utah.gov to identify Utah nonprofits, universities, or school foundations that hire daytime part-time event or community coordinators.
pathways.reality_check: Included as your wildcard option from the pathway table, with a clear constraint gap: irregular event hours often clash with school-hours scheduling and unresolved childcare.
